_doc: Documented reports used as test expectations for the sound physics (audio/PLAN.md 4.8; PDF S.3, C.6). Every OCR line refers to the files registered in GOVERNANCE/library/acquired.json (tmp/library). Quotes are fragments under 15 words. Where the model cannot reproduce a report it says so (model_mismatch) and no default is bent to fit. Tier follows CLAUDE.md: only a non-lead source supporting exactly the claim is 'documented'.

reports.claim: On 1 July a Confederate division approaching Gettysburg from Middletown heard the cannonade when within 4 miles of the town.

evidence.quote: When within 4 miles of the town
evidence.note: report of the division that turned toward Gettysburg at Middletown by Ewell's order; the PDF (T1-109) attributes this to Rodes; the author's name was not read in this session

expectation.reading: model: a single 12-pounder is audible above the day ambient floor at 4 miles (homogeneous atmosphere, upper bound)

reports.claim: A Union officer reports hearing heavy cannonading in front at about 4 miles from Gettysburg on 1 July.

evidence.quote: At the distance of about 4 miles from Gettys- burg, I heard heavy cannonading in front
evidence.note: author not read in this session

evidence.quote: After proceeding about 4 miles, heard cannonading in front

reports.claim: The Twelfth Corps regiment marching on the Gettysburg turnpike first heard cannonading at Two Taverns on the afternoon of 1 July.

evidence.quote: Here the sound of cannonading first reached us.

expectation.note: distance Two Taverns to the firing not taken from a source here

reports.claim: Cannonading of 2 July was reported heard at Harrisburg, 35 to 40 miles north (Harrisburg Evening Telegraph, 3 July 1863, via secondary pages; audio/PLAN.md 4.8).

evidence.source: audio/PLAN.md 4.8 (secondary pages read 2026-10-19: Wynn, Gratz, Lancaster Online)
evidence.note: weak: the newspaper itself was not read; distance is the road estimate

expectation.reading: model: audible with a large margin, spectrum reduced to a low rumble; but the homogeneous model over-predicts range (no turbulence, no ground excess), so this expectation cannot discriminate

reports.claim: Sound of the battle was reported heard in Pittsburgh, about 150 miles (ASA via the PDF C.6); the date is contested (1 July in one source, general in another); the 100 miles of the brief is not the ASA figure.

evidence.source: PDF Appendix C.6 (page 119), citing the Acoustical Society of America and Today I Found Out
evidence.note: weak, contested; no first-hand report read

expectation.reading: model: homogeneous air does not rule it out because it ignores turbulence and ground; the model neither confirms nor disproves the report; any rendering of it is a refraction scenario (plausible-procedural)

reports.claim: On 2 July Ewell's party did not hear Longstreet's artillery signal (PDF Section S.3, C.6; the Ellis attribution and the refraction explanation are unverified).

evidence.source: PDF Section S.3 and C.6 (secondary: Today I Found Out / ASA)
evidence.note: positions and distance not documented here; no number is invented

expectation.reading: the homogeneous model predicts audibility at any distance a party could plausibly have been; the documented non-hearing is NOT reproduced by default; only the shadow_zone scenario (extra loss 25 dB) moves in that direction, as a plausible-procedural scenario

reports.claim: A cannon 1.5 km away is heard about 4.4 s after the flash at 343 m/s (about 20 C).

evidence.note: arithmetic; the plan labels it a hypothesis

reports.claim: The 3 July cannonade was heard at East Cavalry Field as a volume of sound that rolled across the intervening hills.

evidence.source: MI-GB-1889 (Michigan at Gettysburg, address of General James H. Kidd)
evidence.quote: volume of sound volleyed and rolled across the intervening hills

expectation.reading: supports a long rolling tail for the cannonade heard over hills: ridge echo taps and a long reverb tail; no delay value is documented

reports.claim: At Culp's Hill the echoing of the woods increased the roar of the close musketry.

evidence.quote: the echoing of the woods increased the appalling roar

evidence.source: New York at Gettysburg, Final Report vol. 1 (archive.org finalreportonba00chatgoog, not in acquired.json), history of the 78th NY
evidence.quote: For seven hours the woods echoed with the crashing musketry

expectation.reading: supports a woods reverb boost for dense musketry on Culp's Hill: the engine has the hook (woodsAt mask) but no woods mask exists yet, so the boost is not applied by default (open item)

reports.claim: Longstreet's account of 3 July says the thunder on Seminary Ridge was answered by 'the echo from the Federal side'.

evidence.source: BL-3 (Battles and Leaders vol. 3, 'Lee's Right Wing at Gettysburg')
evidence.quote: the echo from the Federal side

expectation.reading: figurative (answering fire), not an acoustic echo: NOT used as evidence for echo

reports.claim: No account read gives a delay, distance or character of an echo at Gettysburg beyond the qualitative statements above; the 7 to 9 s ridge-to-ridge echo in audio/PLAN.md 4.4 is a geometric inference from the DEM, not an account.
